current.text: He moved from Utah to the Lakers and is locked in as their starting center.
The Lakers' backup centers are Kevon Looney and Mamukelashvili, and the team defense depends heavily on Kessler.
The backups behind him are weak, so he should play heavy minutes.
Playing with Luka Doncic should give him plenty of rebounds, pick and roll chances and easy finishes.
Experts expect double-digit rebounds, 12 to 15 points and 2 or more blocks a game, with about six points coming off offensive rebounds.
Experts agree that his jumps in threes, steals, assists and free throw shooting last season came from about five games and will not carry over.
If those gains do not hold, he is not a top 70 player in category leagues.
Experts call him overpriced at a Yahoo rank near 38 and a round 3 cost. Fair value is around rank 60, not in round 3 or 4, and one expert would pay no more than 15 USD for him.
His draft cost in mocks varies a lot, from early round 3 to late round 4. In one auction mock he went for 26 USD.
At an ESPN ADP around 80 he is a fine pick.
He is a good pick for a team that is low on rebounds.
Last season's shoulder surgery is not a concern now. One expert says he could play 80 games.
The Lakers have the second most back-to-backs in the league. Their playoff schedule is 3-4-3 games with a March 28 end, in the bottom half of the league.

durable.text: A rebounds, blocks and FG% center. Nothing else in his profile is strong.
He is a poor free throw shooter, which hurts a team's FT%.
He is below average in points, threes, assists and steals.
His career three-point percentage is 20 to 25%.
An elite rim protector and defensive rebounder, though he may not be able to carry a whole defense on his own.
He had arm or shoulder problems in two of the last three seasons, including shoulder surgery after five games last season.

note: Kessler is a true three-category center: elite blocks and rebounds plus a strong FG%, with a FT% that hurts. That makes him a natural fit for punt FT builds. Yahoo values him at 25 USD (average cost 18.2), while ESPN has 12 USD and he went for 15 USD in our league last season. Experts see his five-game 2025-26 gains in threes, steals and assists as noise, so aim for about 12 to 15 USD and let others pay a round 3 price. Early in the season, check his finger (Yahoo Q), whether he keeps taking threes, and whether his steals stay above his old rate of about 0.5 a game.
